rationale: The first leg is literally the Sloan (1996) working-capital accrual anomaly and the second leg is that same variable rescaled by a monotone [0,1] stability gate, so the composite is close to a rank-preserving re-parameterization of a single known signal rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction — and the earnings-stability conditioning runs against the documented result that the accrual anomaly is strongest among high-volatility/high-arbitrage-risk firms.

Sign conventions are handled correctly (recch/invch/apalch are stated cash-inflow-positive, so a high ratio means cash released from the operating cycle, consistent with the positive expected sign), and pairing cash-flow-statement accrual components with a five-year gross-margin *trend* is a substantively different construct from the archive's level-based balance-sheet accrual plus gross-profitability composite, though coverage of the cash-flow items and the 5-year trend window should be checked for sample-selection artifacts.

The sign is backwards on standard accounting grounds — an increase in taxes payable is an increase in a current liability, which *reduces* accruals and signals higher taxable income relative to book income (a positive earnings-quality indicator in the book-tax-difference literature), so NEG(Δtxp) predicts the opposite of the stated hypothesis; txp is also sparsely populated and economically tiny relative to assets.

Deflating by gross profit makes the ratio non-monotonic and sign-flipping whenever the denominator is small or negative — a firm with a large accrual build and negative gross profit is scored as attractive after the NEG — and a single 1% winsorization does not repair this structural defect, so the "structural interaction" is mostly denominator noise.

The persistence-count construction is a legitimately different functional form from level-based accrual measures and the margin leg guards against the obvious confound (firms liquidating working capital while deteriorating), but the streak leg takes only six discrete values, creating heavy ties and lumpy portfolio composition that will lean on the continuous margin leg to do most of the sorting.

The financing leg is effectively the well-documented net-debt-issuance / external-financing anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Cooper-Gulen-Schill) rather than a novel dimension, and using Δ(lt/ceq) is numerically unstable — negative or near-zero book equity produces sign-flipped extreme values that will dominate the ranks — so a change in net debt scaled by assets would be the minimum fix before this is testable.
